svg.title: Which industries clear the most forest? Agriculture, not timber
svg.desc: A thought bubble shows the common belief that timber and paper cause the most deforestation. A pie chart of the share of global deforestation (2001 to 2023) is then built from the smallest slice: sugar 1%, pulses 2%, plant-based fibres 2%, coffee, cocoa and spices 4%, vegetables, fruits and nuts 5%, roots and tubers 5%, cereals 12%, forestry (timber and paper) 12%, oilseeds 16% and beef 41%. The nine farming slices fuse into 88% against 12% for timber and paper. Data: Singh and Persson (2026), via Our World in Data (CC BY). Simplified: Each slice is named once, in the key, which lights up row by row as its slice sweeps in; the pie itself carries no repeated labels. No explanation overlay: the last frame states its facts (beef is the largest driver at 41%; most soy is fed to livestock).

g.text: Most people believe timber and paper
Which industries clear the most forest?
Share of global deforestation for agriculture, 2001 to 2023
Data: Singh and Persson (2026), via Our World in Data (CC BY)
Beef alone: 41%. Most soy is fed
Timber and paper: only around 1/8 of all deforestation
Beef alone: more than 3 times timber and paper
Farming, especially livestock, not forestry, clears most of the forest.
